newsitem.title: UK: Capital Radio names Mansfield chief exec.
newsitem.headline: Capital Radio names Mansfield chief exec.

text.p: UK music entertainment group Capital Radio said on Thursday that managing director David Mansfield would replace Richard Eyre as chief executive.
Eyre will leave Capital on September 30 to become chief executive of the ITV commercial television network.

Mansfield, 43, has been with Capital for four years, working as commercial director until becoming managing director only two months ago. Eyre, previously managing director, took on the title of chief executive as part of the restructuring announced in May.

Eyre joined Capital six years ago and the company has grown from two radio stations to 12 in that time. It has also expanded into restaurants through the 51 million stg acquisition of My Kinda Town last year.
Capital is also acquiring Virgin Radio in an 87 million stg deal, subject to regulatory approval.
Capital shares fell 13.5p to 516.5p on Thursday morning, but volume was modest.
Capital said Mansfield knew the business well and the succession should be smooth.

"David has been closely involved in the development of strategy and the operations of the business for four years, and the scale of his contribution to the company was acknowledged earlier this year by his promotion to the position of Group Managing Director," said Capital chairman Ian Irvine.

The ITV network commissions and schedules programmes broadcast across its 15 regional franchise constituents. Eyre takes on the vacant post at ITV at a time when the network is seeking to arrest the decline in its viewing share. He knows the advertising industry well, having been media director at the Bartle Bogle Hegarty agency before joining Capital.
Analysts said the appointment was encouraging and should prove popular with advertisers.

"Given his previous experience in the advertising industry at BBH, the appointment is particularly welcome in the signal that it sends to those who fund ITV with their advertising support," said Robert Jolliffe of ABN AMRO Hoare Govett.
"It shows that the network is increasingly keen to focus on advertisers' needs as well as those of its shareholders and viewers," he added.
Eyre will take control of an ITV network dominated by four key players -- United News & Media Plc, Carlton Communications Plc, Granada Group Plc and Scottish Media Group.
Eyre is expected to oversee the transformation of ITV into a limited company as part of moves to streamline its operations.
